Adjusted assessment using SLOOS:
- FOMC tone: Labor market “strong” and activity “solid,” with inflation below 2% and “patient” guidance; policy stance held steady with IOER set to keep funds trading within range—neutral to slightly accommodative.
- SLOOS overlay (April 2019): Banks tightened standards for C&I and construction/land development and tightened other terms across firm sizes. Demand was weaker for HELOCs, credit cards, and other consumer loans, with demand roughly unchanged for subprime mortgages and auto. Foreign banks’ C&I readings and expectations point to softer loan quality. These credit-supply and demand signals imply tighter financial conditions and softer underlying momentum than the FOMC’s headline growth language suggests.
- Net: The positive macro backdrop is tempered by weakening credit demand and tighter standards, shifting the overall tone from mildly positive to near-neutral and reinforcing a cautious stance.
